# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Harper Delgado**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
Member ID: W267205200

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Member Services: 1-888-333-4742

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09**
**Reference number:** POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782
**Member:** Harper Delgado | **Member ID:** W267205200
**Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
**Plan:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Maine
**Governing policy I am citing:** *Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316)* — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf
**This appeal must be received by 2027-02-05.** I am submitting it within that window.

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which the plan denied on 2026-08-09 on the ground that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this surgery is needed.

The notice did not identify which specific documents or findings the plan considered missing. Below I walk through the plan's own published documentation requirements and point to where each item appears in my records. If, after reviewing this, the plan still believes something is absent, I respectfully ask that the plan tell me in writing exactly which item it is and which criterion it applied, so that my surgeon and I can supply it.

---

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. The plan's documentation checklist.** The policy states:

> "Office notes for arthroscopic knee surgery requests should document: o Symptom onset, duration, and severity; o Loss of function and/or limitations; o Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)."

Each of these three items is in my records:

- **Symptom onset, duration, and severity:** 18 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest. My examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Loss of function and/or limitations:** I have locking and giving way of the knee. I cannot squat or kneel, and I am limited to level walking.
- **Type and duration of non-operative management:** supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion for 14 weeks, from 2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02, with 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

**2. Imaging documentation.** The policy states:

> "For all knee arthroscopy requests, the weight-bearing status of all X-rays should be documented in the office notes. If an MRI was performed, the actual MRI report should be included in the office notes as well."

An MRI of my knee was performed on 2026-07-14. It showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with articular cartilage preserved and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1. I am resubmitting the actual MRI report with this appeal so that it is in the file the plan reviews. [If weight-bearing X-rays were obtained, attach the report(s) here and confirm the weight-bearing status as documented in the office notes.]

**3. Arthritis and the weight-bearing X-ray requirement.** The policy states:

> "For meniscus surgery requests, if there is evidence of associated arthritis by history, physical examination or MRI, weight-bearing X-rays are required to further establish the degree of articular cartilage loss."

and:

> "Unless the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, weight-bearing X-rays must show no more than mild arthritis for approval of meniscus procedures. (No more than K-L 2 changes – see grading appendix*)"

Two points from my records are relevant here. First, my MRI records articular cartilage as preserved, at Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 — within the "no more than K-L 2 changes" the policy describes as acceptable, and not evidence of significant articular cartilage loss. Second, the policy's own wording makes the weight-bearing X-ray showing an exception where the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear. My MRI documents a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and my records describe locking and giving way of the knee.

**4. Non-operative treatment.** The policy states:

> "Non-operative treatment for meniscal tears is not required in the following situations:"

That sentence introduces a list of situations that I do not have in front of me in full; I am not going to characterize items I have not seen. Among the situations the policy does describe are:

> "History of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking; Physical examination demonstrates ANY positive meniscal findings on examination or demonstrates evidence of a locked knee (loss of terminal extension); MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus. (Does not include an extruded meniscus or flap tears)"

My records document mechanical symptoms of locking, positive provocative testing on the affected side on physical examination, and an MRI showing a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.

Even setting that aside, I meet the plan's general requirement as well. The policy states:

> "Most meniscal tears WILL require documentation of non-operative treatment as follows:"

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following:"

and the list of qualifying treatments includes:

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection"

My documented non-operative care ran 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02 (20 visits), which is more than the 6 weeks the policy asks for, and it included more than two of the listed modalities: physical therapy modalities, pharmacologic treatment with NSAIDs for 4 months, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13. None of it resolved my symptoms — the injection gave 2 weeks of partial relief, the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief, and my pain has been progressive over 18 months and is unrelieved by rest.

The policy also notes:

> "The required duration of non-operative treatment will vary depending on the surgical procedure - (Example: 6 weeks for meniscectomy, 3 months for diagnostic arthroscopy, 6 months for patellofemoral procedures)."

My 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, combined with 4 months of NSAIDs and an injection, exceeds the 6-week example the policy gives for meniscectomy.

**A note on what I have quoted.** Everything I have placed in quotation marks above is taken word for word from the *Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316)* at the link above. Several of those passages end in a colon and introduce further lists or a grading appendix that I do not have in front of me, so I have not attempted to restate them. If the plan relied on any criterion, list item, or appendix I have not addressed here, I ask that it be identified specifically in the plan's response.

---

## What I am asking the plan to do

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-09 (reference POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782) and authorize knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881.
2. If the plan continues to find the documentation incomplete, state in writing the specific document or clinical element that is missing and the exact criterion from the *Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316)* that was applied, so my surgeon can respond directly.
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with appropriate expertise in orthopedic surgery.
4. Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing.

I am also asking that my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, be permitted to speak with the reviewer if that would help resolve the question.

**Enclosures:** [MRI report dated 2026-07-14], [physical therapy discharge note], [office/operative notes from Dr. Reyes], [injection record dated 2026-05-13], [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-09], [weight-bearing X-ray report(s), if obtained], [any authorization for my surgeon or another representative to act on my behalf].

I am sending this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I may also reach Member Services at 1-888-333-4742. Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Harper Delgado
Member ID: W267205200
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
